tasks.short: Record installation steps and settings, write the procedure document, test it by repeating it, check it, and publish it to the wiki.

steps.what: Web administrator records installation steps and settings while installing
Web administrator documents installation or configuration procedures with screenshots

loop.input: The installation script or recorded command history, and the administrator's notes.
loop.output: A draft step-by-step procedure in the team's format.
loop.check: Every command or setting in the draft must appear in the script or recorded session, or it is dropped; the administrator reads every step and edits it.
loop.stop: One draft per procedure; if rejected, the administrator writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A script shows what runs, not why or what to check between steps.

steps.what: Web administrator tests the procedure by repeating it on a test server
Web administrator checks the final procedure
Web administrator publishes the procedure to the team wiki

tasks.design: Installations done by script, about 60%, keep the script and its settings in the repository ({OTHER}), so steps are not noted by hand; manual installs record the command history. A bounded step drafts the procedure from the script or history; commands not found there are dropped and the administrator edits every step. Scripted procedures are tested by a pipeline run on a test server instead of repeating them by hand. Once checked, the procedure is published to the wiki ({DOCS}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Steps were noted by hand during installs and procedures written afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Installs run from scripts; language models draft procedures checked against them.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor installers with screens cannot be scripted.
tasks.human_edge: Writing down the one step that always goes wrong.
tasks.altitude: The administrator edits procedures instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review.
Language models can draft procedures that can be checked against a script or command history.

assumptions: Boundary: from the installation done to the procedure published; the installation itself is outside.
Input contract: scripts kept in the repository; fallback is notes.
Scenario: about 60% of installations are scripted.
research_questions: Do repeated installations succeed first time more often?

incremental.description: Web administrator keeps the procedure template current.

approvals.approved_version: The procedure as checked by the administrator in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly vendor installers with screens; high: mostly scripted installs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide what to test and the acceptance criteria, write test cases, set up test runs in the pipeline, document the test procedure, and review results with developers.

steps.what: Web administrator decides what to test and the acceptance criteria
Web administrator develops testing routines by writing test cases

loop.input: The acceptance criteria and the pages under test.
loop.output: Draft automated browser tests, one or more per criterion.
loop.check: Each test must run green on the current site and name the criterion it covers, or it is dropped; the administrator reviews every test before it is kept.
loop.stop: Up to three repair attempts per failing test; then the administrator writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Recording clicks gives brittle tests without the checks that matter.

steps.what: Web administrator sets up test runs in the build pipeline
Web administrator documents the test procedure
Web administrator reviews test results with developers

tasks.design: A test agent drafts automated browser tests from the acceptance criteria; tests that do not run green or do not name a criterion are dropped, and the administrator reviews every test. Pipeline templates ({OTHER}) run the tests on each release instead of setting up runs by hand, and the test procedure page is generated from the test definitions. Deciding what to test and reviewing results stay with the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test cases were written in spreadsheets and run by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Test agents draft browser tests that can be checked by running them.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted tests may test the wrong thing while passing.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which user path must never break.
tasks.altitude: The administrator reviews tests instead of writing each one.

reach.learn: Whether tests find problems before release.

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents let a model write test plans and tests and repair failing ones.
In a randomised trial, 16 experienced open-source developers were 19% slower with early-2025 AI tools; the authors call it outdated.

assumptions: Boundary: from the release planned to results reviewed; fixing defects is outside.
Input contract: test tool and pipeline available; fallback is spreadsheets and manual runs.
The administrator reviews every drafted test.
research_questions: How many drafted tests are kept after review?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex pages where drafted tests often fail; high: simple pages with clear criteria.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan home page campaigns with marketing, schedule banner rotation, prepare banners in several sizes, and track campaign results.

steps.what: Web administrator develops the home page marketing plan with the marketing team
Web administrator implements advertisement rotation by editing the home page by hand
Web administrator prepares banners and texts in several sizes
Web administrator tracks campaign results in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Home page slots in the content system ({CMS}) take banners with start and end dates and rotate them on schedule, so the administrator does not edit the page by hand at each change. Banner templates per slot size let one design be exported in all sizes. Click-through per slot and campaign shows in the analytics dashboard ({BI}) instead of a spreadsheet. Planning campaigns with marketing stays with the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Banners were swapped by hand and results tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Content systems schedule slot content; dashboards show clicks per slot.
tasks.still_hard: Print advertising follows its own deadlines.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which message gets the top of the home page.

reach.learn: Whether banners go live on time.

evidence.claim: Content systems can schedule slot content with start and end dates.
Click tracking with cookies needs visitors' consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the campaign planned to results tracked; print production is outside.
Input contract: scheduled slots set up in the content system; fallback is editing by hand.
Planning with marketing does not change.
research_questions: Do banners go live and come down on time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few campaigns with mostly print work; high: frequent web campaigns.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect requirements, research options, compare them on costs and criteria, test a trial installation, write the recommendation, and present it.

steps.what: Web administrator collects requirements from teams
Web administrator researches server hardware or software options and vendor specifications
Web administrator evaluates options on costs and criteria in a spreadsheet
Web administrator tests a trial installation
Web administrator writes the recommendation
Web administrator recommends the choice to the IT manager

tasks.design: A standard evaluation template with weighted criteria, security requirements and a five-year cost model ({SPREADSHEET}) replaces building a comparison from scratch each time, and the recommendation template takes the scores and costs from it. Earlier evaluations are kept in the team wiki so known options start with their specs. Collecting requirements, testing trials and recommending stay with the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each evaluation started from a blank spreadsheet and document.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and earlier evaluations shorten comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor specifications are hard to compare like for like.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which vendor will still support the product in five years.

evidence.claim: Weighted evaluation templates with cost models are a standard way to compare IT options.
Products with digital elements sold in the EU must meet cyber security requirements.

assumptions: Boundary: from the need raised to the choice recommended; buying is outside.
Input contract: template kept by the IT team; fallback is a blank spreadsheet.
Trials and the recommendation meeting do not change.
The IT manager's time does not change.

incremental.description: Web administrator keeps the evaluation template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new kind of product; high: a repeat evaluation of known options.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web administrator keeps deciding tests, planning campaigns and recommending purchases; hand-noted installs, spreadsheet test cases, banner swaps and blank comparisons shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An administrator with more time on reliability.
